title: Variables and Data Types
instructions: A variable is a named box that holds a value. Every box has a type that decides what it can hold.
- int — whole numbers, like 33. Print with %d.
- float and double — numbers with a decimal, like 5.9. Print with %f.
- char — ONE character in single quotes, like 'A'. Print with %c.
Secret truth: a char is really just a number underneath (its ASCII code). 'A' is 65. That's why you can print the same char two ways.
The %d, %f, %c are 'format specifiers' — they tell printf how to show the value.
task: Add a line that prints the char grade as a NUMBER, so the output ends with:  grade as a number = 65
hint:
Use %d on the same char variable:

    printf("grade as a number = %d\n", grade);
expected_output:
age = 33
grade = A
grade as a number = 65
